title: Concise SDK starter journeys and edge cases (sketch)
summary: A compact working sketch that defines three short starter journeys for new SDK users (CLI-first, local-app, and serverless), a set of micro-labs to practice failure modes, and a pragmatic checklist for telemetry and rollback behavior. Focus is on minimum friction onboarding + early detection of regressions.
content:
CONCISE SDK STARTER JOURNEYS + EDGE CASES (WORKING SKETCH)

Status: draft — quick iteration notes, TODOs scattered. Audience: SDK writers, docs engineer, developer advocates. Goal: produce a 6–10 minute first-run experience that covers normal flow + two common failure modes so users leave confident.

Goals and constraints
- <Goal> 1-2 minute install + hello world that streams output.
- <Goal> show both sync and streaming paths quickly.
- <Goal> micro-labs: teach recovery from token errors and graceful fallback when streaming not available.
- Constraint: keep examples language-agnostic but provide Py + JS snippets.

Persona(s)
- Frontend engineer prototyping a chat widget (wants streaming).
- Backend engineer wiring a serverless endpoint (wants simple sync).
- Platform engineer evaluating telemetry and cost knobs.

Starter journeys (3 compact flows)
1) CLI-first loop (local, fastest path) — 4 steps
   - install: pip/npm quick command
     - pip: pip install redwood-inference-sdk  # experimental pkg name
     - npm: npm i @redwood/inference-sdk
   - set API key env var: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
   - quick command: redwood chat --model=redwood-mini --prompt="Hello" --stream
   - expected: streaming tokens appear in terminal. If stream fallback occurs, command prints single JSON response.
   - micro-check: exit code 0 for success, 2 for auth error, 3 for network timeout.

2) Local app (React dev flow) — 5 steps, focus on CORS & streaming polyfill
   - copy minimal snippet into app; use SDK client that multiplexes fetch + websockets depending on environment.
   - example pattern (JS):
     const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
     const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-mini', messages: [...] });
     for await (const chunk of stream) { renderChunk(chunk); }
   - notes: suggest using the provided streaming polyfill in browsers that block chunked responses. Provide fallback: poll endpoint for status & partial tokens.

3) Serverless route (fast deploy to lambda/Cloud Run) — 6 steps
   - skeleton: handler validates input, calls SDK sync generate API, returns minimal JSON.
   - recommend short timeout (2–3s) for generator sync by default; offer streaming-presign endpoint for long responses.
   - include instrumentation: increment metric sdk.requests, attach model, prompt_len, tokens_generated.

Mini-labs (hands-on checkpoints, 10–20 minute each)
- Lab A: Token auth failure recovery (5 steps)
  - intentionally use expired key, observe error shape, check SDK error.code === 'auth_expired', then call getNewKey() flow and retry with exponential backoff.
- Lab B: Stream fallback test
  - run demo behind corporate proxy that strips chunked transfer; ensure app falls back to polling endpoint and UI shows progress bar instead of streaming text.
- Lab C: Cost spike simulation
  - send long context loops, assert telemetry exposes tokens_by_request metric and alerts if 95th percentile unit cost > threshold.

Edge cases + anti-patterns (short list)
- Unbounded retries after 5xx: provide default retry policy: 3 attempts with jitter and exponential backoff.
- Blocking on full response for long-running generation: recommend using streaming + UI progressive rendering.
- Overly small batch sizes in heavy throughput apps: default shard/batch config tuned for general web workloads; docs show how to tune.
- Local dev using prod keys: warn and provide short-lived dev tokens via dev server helper.

Telemetry & SDK contracts (practical, minimal)
- Telemetry events (names): sdk.request.start, sdk.request.end, sdk.stream.chunk, sdk.error.(auth|network|server), sdk.retry.
- Minimum attributes: model, region, api_plan (free/paid), prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, request_id.
- Expose an opt-out config: { telemetry: { enabled: true|false } } and a hook to add custom dimensions.
- Local dev: default telemetry disabled unless REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=1 to avoid accidental signal leakage.

Failures and rollback playbook (for app authors)
- Detectable signals: repeated 5xx, auth_expired, streaming_fallback_rate > 10% in 5m window.
- Immediate actions: fall back to smaller model variant, enable cached prefixes, reduce max_tokens.
- Emergency fallback: return cached human-friendly message and queue async retry; emit incident telemetry and alert.

Quick checklist for docs pages (what to produce from this sketch)
- 1x CLI quickstart (60–90s): install -> set key -> run a streaming chat -> view errors.
- 1x React quickstart (3–5 min): copy/paste minimal app + streaming polyfill link.
- 1x Serverless sample repo (link to GH template) with instrumentation + env var patterns.
- 3 micro-labs with step-by-step steps and expected outputs + troubleshooting hints.
- Troubleshooting section: auth, proxy, streaming, cost.

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide default stream fallback mechanism: polling vs websocket upgrade. (TODO: sync with serving-runtime team)
- Should SDK auto-inject model cost estimate per request? (ops + billing input needed)
- Provide concrete example of telemetry export to Datadog/Prometheus? (ask SRE)

Next steps (owner: Aisha)
- Draft the CLI quickstart doc + runnable demo image (due: 2024-10-17).
- Pair with Runtime team to confirm stream fallback design (book 1-hour).
- Create three GH templates for CLI, React, Serverless (minimal license header) and wire CI to run quick smoke tests.

Notes to self (fragmented / rough)
- Keep code examples tiny. Avoid mixing too many SDK features in the initial page.
- Prefer concrete commands that people can cut-and-paste.
- Add a tiny FAQ block: "why is stream falling back?" + "what to do when seeing 429s".

---
Working draft ends. This file is a sketch intended for rapid conversion into more formal quickstarts and micro-labs.
